correctness.rationale: For n>=2 and positive q_j with r_k=sum_{j<=k}q_j>=k, the open chamber D_n has positive Lebesgue measure; its boundary is null. The source substitution w_1^2=q_1 z_1^2-(q_1-1)z_2^2, w_j=z_j for j>=2 maps the interior bijectively to itself. The inverse gives sqrt(q_1)|det(dz/dw)|=w_1/sqrt(w_1^2+(q_1-1)w_2^2)<=1, strictly <1 at every interior point if q_1>1 since w_2>0. The transformed quadratic form has coefficients (1,q_1+q_2-1,q_3,...), first prefix 1 and later prefixes r_k. Summation by parts gives transformed Q(w)-sum w_j^2=sum_{k=2}^n(r_k-k)(w_k^2-w_{k+1}^2)>=0, with w_{n+1}=0. Hence integral equality is impossible if q_1>1. If q_1=1 the map is identity, and Q(z)-sum z_j^2=sum_{k=1}^n(r_k-k)(z_k^2-z_{k+1}^2); each square gap is strictly positive on D_n. Equality of the two positive integrals forces every prefix defect zero, whence q_j=1 for all j. Conversely all ones gives equality. For n=1, Gaussian rescaling gives equality for all q_1>0, confirming the sharp dimension boundary. In a nondegenerate orthoscheme, q_j=beta_j^2 and r_k=|b_k|^2. Zwierzyński Proposition 3.2 Eq. (18) identifies the exact local sector ratio as a positive n-constant divided by beta_1 I(q), so equality is equivalent to the integral equality; beta_j>0 then forces beta_j=1, unique standard cube-flag orthoscheme up to orthogonal congruence. Independent symbolic identities in 14 finite dimensions, 2250 exact-rational admissible pointwise tests, 6 exact two-dimensional integral calculations, and independent Git tree reconstruction corroborate but are not substituted for the universal argument.
residual_risks: The conclusion is limited to the local analytic orthoscheme step; no global equality classification for arbitrary polytopes is proved.
No quantitative stability modulus is proved, and n=1 is genuinely non-rigid.
Finite arithmetic and two-dimensional integral checks do not establish unbounded n; the all-n assertion rests on the exact positivity argument.

value.rationale: The precise local equality geometry is intrinsically motivated: in the new sharp dimension-free surface-area theorem, every flag contributes an orthoscheme sector quotient, so knowing whether nonstandard orthoschemes attain the sharp local constant is a natural necessary ingredient in studying global equality and quantitative stability. The result identifies a dimension boundary (n=1 non-rigid; n>=2 rigid) and exact all-dimensional extremal geometry, rather than an arbitrary numerical slice. Its analytic derivation is routine from the prior paper and is not an independent original advance, but the equality classification is a mathematically useful structural interpretation of the sharp bound. No global rigidity or deficit modulus is claimed.

final_claim: For every integer n>=2 and positive q_1,...,q_n whose partial sums r_k>=k, normalized ordered Gaussian integral sqrt(q_1) I(q)=I(1,...,1) if and only if q_1=...=q_n=1. Consequently for nondegenerate orthoschemes B=conv(0,b_1,...,b_n) with mutually orthogonal successive edges, b_k=(beta_1,...,beta_k,0,...), beta_j>0 and |b_k|>=sqrt(k), equality in the local source surface-to-unit-ball-sector estimate holds iff beta_j=1 for every j, standard cube-flag orthoscheme up to orthogonal transformation. For n=1 equality holds for all q_1>0 and rigidity fails; no global polytope uniqueness or quantitative stability is asserted.
